description: This circular chart visually organizes and compares the components of medical ethics, structured around three primary principles: Beneficence (depicted in blue), Autonomy (in green), and Justice (in orange), with a smaller purple segment labeled Non-Maleficence. The chart is divided into multiple slices, each representing a specific ethical duty or consideration. The largest segment, Beneficence, contains 11 subcategories including “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues,” “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interests,” “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest,” “Ethical research,” “Open Discussion and Fair Charging of Fees,” “Comply with Laws and Regulations,” “Recognize the Responsibility of the Occupation,” and “Promote the Health of Community.” The Autonomy segment, in green, includes 7 subcategories: “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” “Professional Relationship with Patients and Their Relatives,” “Keep Confidential Patient’s Information,” “Maintain Truthful, Factual Communication,” “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed, Freedom of Choice,” and “Respect the Decision-making of Incompetent/Competent Patient.” The Justice segment, in orange, contains 5 subcategories: “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” “Treat Patients Fairly and Equally,” “Prevent Patient from Harm,” and “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care.” The Non-Maleficence segment, in purple, includes 3 subcategories: “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain,” and “Prevent Patient from Harm.” The chart appears to be a conceptual or educational visualization rather than a quantitative data representation, as no percentages or numerical values are displayed within the slices. There is no legend, and the slices are arranged in a clockwise order, with the largest segment (Beneficence) occupying the left half of the circle, followed by Autonomy on the right, and Justice and Non-Maleficence occupying the top right and bottom right quadrants respectively. The chart uses distinct colors for each principle to aid visual differentiation, but no slice is visually emphasized or exploded.
